subject: Step-down prepay conversion and true-up cadence
messages:
From: Sara Walton <sara.walton@luminahc.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Tran <alex.tran@luminahc.com>
Date: 2026-09-12T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Switching to annual prepay — questions on discount schedule & true-up

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — Lumina’s engineering and finance teams are aligned on moving from our current monthly billing to an annual prepay in order to lock in better unit economics. Before we present this to our CFO I have a few practical questions on how Redwood structures multi-year/annual prepay discounts and the true-up mechanism on usage. Specifically: 

- Do you support a step-down discount (higher discount on year 1 committed volume, reduced in year 2 if we add more capacity)?
- How do you handle under-utilization in the first 90 days — true-up, credit, or rollover?
- If we commit to a 24-month term with an annual invoice, can we do staged invoicing (50% at signing, 50% at the 12-month mark)?
- Any precedent for a small onboarding credit or ramp protection for the first 3 months while we integrate?

Appreciate any concrete examples or a sample term sheet we can share internally. Attaching our initial procurement timeline in a follow-up.

Best,
Sara
Sara Walton
VP Finance (acting CFO)
Lumina Health

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Walton <sara.walton@luminahc.com>
Cc: Alex Tran <alex.tran@luminahc.com>
Date: 2026-09-12T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Switching to annual prepay — questions on discount schedule & true-up

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Great to hear you’re moving toward prepay. I put together a concise proposal below and attached a draft term sheet (Lumina_TermSheet_v3.pdf) for review. High-level answers and an example step-down schedule: 

1) Step-down discount structure (example for a 24-month, $1.2M ARR-equivalent commitment):
   - Year 1 prepaid: 18% list discount on compute/embedding unit rates (applied to committed volume)
   - Year 2 prepaid: 12% list discount (if you renew the second year at committed baseline)
   - If you expand committed volume mid-term, incremental volume gets a 10% add-on discount or can be rebundled into a new blended rate.

2) Under-utilization / ramp protection:
   - First 90 days: two options — (a) monthly true-up with credits for usage below a 70% utilization threshold, or (b) one-time ramp credit equal to 5% of the first-year prepay if utilization <60% at day 90. The term sheet includes the credit option by default; we can flip to a pure true-up if you prefer.

3) Invoicing cadence:
   - Standard: annual invoice at signing for the contracted year. 
   - We can support staged invoices for multi-year deals: 50% at signing, 50% at 12 months for a 24-month commitment — we’ve used this with enterprise accounts.

4) Onboarding credit:
   - We can offer a one-time onboarding credit (applied against tokens) equal to $10k for integration assistance, or equivalently 3% of year-1 prepay value, whichever is greater.

Next steps if this looks reasonable: 1) I’ll loop in Ben (sales lead) and Marissa (contracts) to put the draft term sheet into DocuSign; 2) you share your preferred invoicing/legal contacts; 3) finalize the ramp metric (we recommend the 60% threshold with a 5% credit).

Attachment: Lumina_TermSheet_v3.pdf (draft - highlights: discount table, true-up options, invoicing schedule, SLA credit language).

Cheers,

Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: Sara Walton <sara.walton@luminahc.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Tran <alex.tran@luminahc.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Switching to annual prepay — questions on discount schedule & true-up

Kimberly — this is super helpful, thanks. A few clarifications our procurement team will want spelled out in the term sheet: 

- For the step-down: can you show a worked example with actual unit rates (tokens/embedding units) so our FP&A can model dollars per feature?
- True-up: prefer a deterministic monthly true-up rather than an opaque credit — can you convert the 5% credit option into an automated monthly true-up that applies a pro-rata credit on the subsequent invoice?
- Onboarding credit: acceptable, but we’d prefer the onboarding credit to be invoiced as a negative line item on the first invoice (rather than a token grant).
- Can we request 60-day price protection on the quoted schedule once we sign the term sheet? CFO will want to lock pricing while finance runs internal approvals.

Also, one operational ask: we need retention/audit log windows documented (HIPAA considerations). Can Marissa include the retention commitment in the SOW? Alex (cc) is our technical lead and will need the SLA and KV-cache warming guidance for ramp.

Thanks — I’ll aim to get this in front of our CFO by end of next week if we can lock pricing and the true-up.

—Sara

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Sara Walton <sara.walton@luminahc.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Switching to annual prepay — questions on discount schedule & true-up

Sara / Kimberly — good thread. Quick note from my side on commercial flexibility: 

- We can provide a worked unit-rate example in the term sheet (tokens/embeddings) — I’ll attach a short pricing appendix showing list vs discounted rates and a modeled monthly spend for a 6/12/24 month ramp.
- Agree on deterministic monthly true-up — proposal: monthly reconciliation, with any shortfall credited against the next invoice within 30 days. If the contract is prepaid, we apply a pro-rata token credit as a negative invoice line (matches Sara’s ask).
- For price protection: we’ll hold quoted rates for 60 days from term-sheet sign-off. If you need 90, we can discuss extending with a small commitment increase.
- Onboarding credit: we’ll do it as a negative line on the first invoice per Lumina’s preference (not as token grant).
- As a one-time concession for a strategic 24-month commit, I can approve a $15k onboarding support credit and an operational SLA addendum that documents KV-warming and prioritized capacity for the first 90 days. 

Marissa — can you prepare the SOW language for data-retention and the DocuSign-ready term sheet? Sara — if you share your procurement contact I’ll get our billing team aligned for staged invoicing.

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Walton <sara.walton@luminahc.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Updated term sheet and SOW (DocuSign link)

Hi Sara — I reviewed Kimberly/Ben’s proposals and updated the term sheet and SOW to capture Lumina’s asks. Changes/highlights: 

- Pricing appendix: includes example unit rates at list and discounted tiers (see attached SOW-Lumina-2026.xlsx).
- Monthly true-up: now written as a deterministic monthly reconciliation where any under-utilization is shown as a negative invoice line for the subsequent invoice period. Language calls for reconciliation within 30 days and clear formula in Appendix B.
- Onboarding credit: added as a negative first-invoice line for $15,000.
- Price protection: clause added — quoted pricing guaranteed for 60 days after sign-off on this term sheet.
- Data retention/audit logs: SOW includes 7-year audit-log retention option (HIPAA addendum) — operational details in Appendix C.
- SLA & ramp ops: operational playbook attached; includes KV cache warming guidance and a 90-day priority queue for capacity.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/Envelope/ABC-9876 (term sheet + SOW bundle). 

Sara — once you confirm the procurement contact we’ll create the DocuSign envelope for signature. Happy to take any redlines but trying to keep the commercial terms as-is to avoid delaying CFO review.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Contracts Counsel | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: SOW-Lumina-2026.xlsx

From: Alex Tran <alex.tran@luminahc.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sara Walton <sara.walton@luminahc.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Quick technical confirm — KV cache and ramp guidance

Marissa / Kimberly — quick confirm on the KV-warming guidance: during the first 30 days we should expect Redwood to provide prioritized cache warm-up for the routes in the SOW; is that correct? Also, any recommended pre-warming batch sizes or startup concurrency targets you’ve seen work well for health-care NLP workloads?

If you can put the two recommended numbers in the SOW appendix (startup concurrency = X, pre-warm batch = Y), that will help our infra team plan the rollout.

Thanks,
Alex Tran
Principal Engineer, Lumina Health
alex.tran@luminahc.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Walton <sara.walton@luminahc.com>, Alex Tran <alex.tran@luminahc.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-16T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Step-down prepay conversion and true-up cadence — next steps

Sara / Alex — glad we’re converging. Quick confirmation and next steps: 

- Invoice timing: we’ll issue the first negative-line invoice (reflecting the $15k onboarding credit) within 5 business days of DocuSign completion. For staged 24-month flow we’ll schedule 50% at signing / 50% at month 12 per the term sheet.
- True-up automation: finance will run the monthly reconciliation and apply negative line items to the subsequent invoice within 30 days; we’ll include the reconciliation file in each billing packet.
- KV-warm guidance (to include in Appendix C): recommended startup concurrency = 16 workers; pre-warm batch = 50 requests per route — conservative defaults for privacy-sensitive NLP inference. We’ll tweak these once traffic patterns are observed.
- Pricing lock: rates held for 60 days from sign-off.

I’ll open the DocuSign envelope once I have Lumina’s procurement contact (billing@luminahc.com or a direct procurement person) and then Ben/Marissa will finalize the billing ops handoff. Please reply with your procurement contact and I’ll move the envelope.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
